opportunities.title: [security/medium] Command Injection Risk in MCP prepare_upload Returned Shell Command via Unescaped filename
opportunities.excerpt:
<!-- security-pipeline:fingerprint=2f9f34bca9aae487 -->
**Severity:** medium  
**CWE:** CWE-78  
**Location:** `src/mcp.ts:370`  
**Last seen:** https://github.com/eovidiu/wa-gatweay/actions/runs/45959354643

### Description
The MCP prepare_upload tool embeds the caller-supplied filename parameter inside double quotes in a curl shell command string returned to the AI assistant. While double quotes are stripped via filename.replace(/"/g, ""), shell metacharacters that remain active inside double quotes ($(...), backticks, $VAR, and backslashes) are not escaped or prevented. If an untrusted WhatsApp message performs indirect prompt injection causing the assistant to pass a crafted filename and execute the returned curl command, arbitrary shell commands can execute on the MCP client host.

### Evidence
src/mcp.ts:368-377 (prepare_upload): line 370 constructs local = filename ? `"${filename.replace(/"/g, "")}"` : "<path to the file>" and interpolates it into `curl -sS --fail-with-body -X PUT -H 'content-type: application/octet-stream' --data-binary @${local} '${u.url}'` at line 377.

### Remediation
Single-quote escape the filename for POSIX shells (e.g., `'${filename.replace(/'/g, "'\\''")}'`) or reject filenames containing shell metacharacters, and instruct the client to pass the path safely without shell interpolation.
opportunities.evidenceLevel: reported open issue; neither validated demand nor endorsement

opportunities.title: [security/high] SSRF via Unvalidated Outbound Media URLs in Cloud API and MCP send_media
opportunities.excerpt:
<!-- security-pipeline:fingerprint=8821c2e2bc32d74c -->
**Severity:** high  
**CWE:** CWE-918  
**Location:** `src/session.ts:2505`  
**Last seen:** https://github.com/eovidiu/wa-gatweay/actions/runs/45959354643

### Description
Both the WhatsApp Cloud API endpoint (POST /api/:phoneNumberId/messages) and the MCP send_media tool accept arbitrary http:// or https:// media URLs and pass them to Baileys via toMediaInput(media), which returns { url: media } without validating destination IP addresses, hostnames, DNS resolution, or HTTP redirects. An authenticated bot token holder, an OAuth-authorized MCP client, or an attacker leveraging indirect prompt injection via inbound WhatsApp messages can force the gateway to fetch internal Docker/LAN services, loopback endpoints, or cloud metadata URLs and exfiltrate the response as a WhatsApp media or document message.

### Evidence
src/routes.ts:200 (POST /:phoneNumberId/messages) -> src/cloud.ts:132 (parseCloudSendRequest) -> src/cloud.ts:84 (mediaRef accepts any non-empty string in link/id); OR src/mcp.ts:387 (send_media tool accepts any url: z.string().url()). Both flow into Session.sendCloud -> Session.sendImage / Session.sendCloudMedia (src/session.ts:1425) -> toMediaInput (src/session.ts:2505), which returns { url: media } for any string starting with http:// or https:// and passes it to sock.sendMessage.

### Remediation
Validate and resolve outbound media URLs before passing them to Baileys: enforce https:// (or explicit allowlist), resolve DNS and block loopback (127.0.0.0/8, ::1), RFC1918 private ranges, link-local/metadata ranges (169.254.0.0/16, fe80::/10), and CGNAT/ULA ranges, disable or re-validate redirects, and fetch the bounded response into a Buffer using the validated IP/socket before passing it to sock.sendMessage.
opportunities.evidenceLevel: reported open issue; neither validated demand nor endorsement

opportunities.title: Package Osborn's agents, skills and hooks as a Claude Code plugin (one source for every runtime)
opportunities.excerpt:
## Goal
Osborn's agent framework (named agents, skills, hooks, chain order and the patterns around them) should follow the Claude Code **plugin** layout, so one folder is the single source that every runtime loads:
- the Osborn voice runtime (Agent SDK),
- the `issue-agent` GitHub Actions run,
- local Claude Code sessions in this repo,
- and anyone else who installs it.

Changing a file in that folder changes all of them. No copies to maintain.

## Today
- Named agents (researcher, reasoner, planner, writer, tester, steward, reviewer) are TypeScript literals in `agent/src/claude-llm.ts` (`NAMED_AGENTS`); roles and chains in `agent/src/agent-store.ts`. Only the steward reads its prompt from a file (`agent/src/prompts/steward.md`, shared with `.claude/agents/steward.md`).
- Bundled skills live in `agent/.claude/skills/`; repo skills in `.claude/skills/`.
- Hooks: repo hooks in `.claude/settings.json` + `.claude/hooks/`; the chain advance and role write gate run in-process in the Osborn runtime.
- The `issue-agent` run therefore loads the steward, the pre-PR reviewer and the repo hooks, but not the other agents, the bundled skills or the chain.

## Ask
1. Check the current Claude Code plugin format against the official docs (manifest, agents/, skills/, hooks/, commands/, MCP) and whether the Agent SDK and `claude-code-action` (`--plugin-dir` / plugin inputs) load it the same way.
2. Audit each existing skill, agent and hook against that format and list what does not follow it.
3. Propose the folder layout and the smallest changes so Osborn's runtime and the cloud run load the same plugin folder. Name what cannot be file-based (in-process callbacks) and the workaround.

Related design notes: agent instructions move from TypeScript into plain files (steward pattern), chain order lives in the `chain-after-<role>.md` files, and cloud chain enforcement uses a PostToolUse plus Stop hook. Related: #626, #629, #453.

## Done when
- A written audit and target layout are posted on this issue.
- The plugin loads in a local Claude Code session and in one `issue-agent` run, and both list the same agents and skills.
opportunities.evidenceLevel: reported open issue; neither validated demand nor endorsement

opportunities.title: Heartbeats: Claude Code hooks package that writes a JSONL outbox
opportunities.excerpt:
Part of #87, from the agent heartbeats discussion (#8). Needs #88.

## Why
Claude Code hooks fire on events and carry no prose of their own. A hook has to turn each event into a heartbeat quickly, because some run inline on every tool call, and it must never break the session. Appending to a local file first means a heartbeat survives Mission Control restarting or the laptop going offline; #90 sends it later.

## What exists
Nothing in this repository. flight-rules had a `PostToolUse` heartbeat hook (a detached child process, about 55 ms) until v2.0.0 removed it with the rest of its board integration. This package starts fresh and doesn't port that code. flight-rules may depend on this package later, so it is a standalone package rather than part of the web app or Mission Control.

## Scope
- A new workspace package in `packages/hooks` with a `dash-hooks` bin. Each Claude Code hook event gets a subcommand that reads the hook payload on stdin.
- Event to heartbeat, using the statuses from #88:
  - `UserPromptSubmit`: the agent is working.
  - `PreToolUse` on `AskUserQuestion`: needs input, with `question` and its options copied verbatim.
  - `Notification`: a permission prompt needs input, with the notification text copied verbatim as `question`.
  - `Stop`: the turn ended. Read the transcript at `transcript_path` and put the last assistant message, trimmed, in `summary`.
  - `SubagentStart` and `SubagentStop`: heartbeats for the subagent, with its `agent_id` and the parent's `session_id`.
  - `SessionStart` and `SessionEnd`: the session's first and last heartbeats.
- **Outbox.** One JSONL file per session under `$XDG_STATE_HOME/dash/outbox/` (falling back to `~/.local/state/dash/outbox/`). `seq` comes from a small per-session counter file updated under a lock, because a parent and its subagents fire hooks in parallel and must never reuse a number.
- **Never fail the session.** Any error exits 0 and goes to a log file next to the outbox. A transcript that can't be read gives a heartbeat with no `summary`, not no heartbeat.
- **Hook registration.** Ship the Claude Code hooks configuration with the package.
- Tests: a recorded payload for each event produces the expected heartbeat; concurrent writers in one session get distinct, increasing `seq` values; an unreadable transcript still writes a heartbeat.

## Open questions
- How the package reaches a machine: pu

inboundFeedback.title: [Agent trial] Maintainer assignment: preserve SIGINT child exit status in cage relay
inboundFeedback.body:
Maintainer-assigned real engineering task for the resident. This is not external adoption feedback.

Observed on the current source: src/cage/relay.js exits with 143 when its child terminates with SIGINT. The relay's stated contract is to leave with the child's exit status; the conventional shell status for SIGINT is 128 + 2 = 130.

Reproduction (run from the repository, Node on Linux/macOS):

```js
import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
const result = spawnSync(process.execPath, [
  'src/cage/relay.js', '/tmp/unused-agenthub-task.sock', '0', '--',
  process.execPath, '-e', "process.kill(process.pid, 'SIGINT')"
], { encoding: 'utf8', timeout: 5000 });
console.log(result.status); // observed 143; expected 130
```

The unused Unix socket is never contacted by this reproduction. Port 0 requests an ephemeral loopback port. No external service or credentials are needed.

Acceptance:
- Independently reproduce the baseline failure with a new regression test.
- Correct source behavior without editing existing tests, the controller, workflows or manifests.
- Preserve ordinary numeric child exit codes, SIGTERM=143 and SIGKILL=137.
- The exact regression must fail before the change and pass after it; the complete existing suite must pass.
- Save a candidate branch/PR with actual execution evidence. Do not claim success from a proposed patch or model review.

Start with src/cage/relay.js. Do not pursue the earlier unverified port-binding-race hypothesis for this task. If blocked, record the actual tool error and checkpoint.

This task tests one useful repair, not autonomous general intelligence or adoption.
